text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:

- Planning Minister Terje Roed-Larsen, former Middle East mediator, quit the Norwegian government on Wednesday amid a scandal over alleged irregularities in a share-option deal he profited from 10 years ago.

- Opposition parties in parliament say the Labour government's position is weaker after Roed-Larsen's resignation. Jan Petersen, leader of the Conservative Party, criticised Prime Minister Thorbjoern Jagland's handling of the scandal.

- A state school in Kristiansand, southern Norway, will arrange auctions, jumble sales and lotteries to raise money for school books. Leif Hopland, head of education in the Kristiansand municipality, is critical of the arrangements. He says that school books are the responsibility of the state.
- Former Planning Minister Terje Roed-Larsen risks imprisonment if allegations that he back dated a contract for share-options in fishing company Fideco A/S in 1986 are proven.
- Prime Minister Jagland said on Wednesday that as the scandal regarding Terje Roed-Larsen developed, Roed-Larsen had no other choice than to resign.
